semantic_adjudication.reason: NL2's quoted clause ('and turned off with the keyOff signal') requires a direct keyOff-triggered Operate->Off transition. The exact bound facts show transition:line:22 (Operate->Off) has triggers=[] and guard=R45RouteToken==7, a token set only by the three child-scoped keyOff transitions (line:16/17/18) exiting to Operate's local final pseudostate. This is a genuine trigger-set mismatch on the carrier transition. However, the exact source facts also show the keyOff event is consumed and does drive an eventual Off transition through this compiled two-step (child-exit + token-guard) mechanism, giving rise to a competent rebuttal reading that the overall behavior realizes the required single semantic transition, even though it is not literally structured as one directly-triggered edge. This alternative is grounded in the exact supplied transition/guard/trigger facts (not mere possibility), so it survives as a rebutting defeater rather than being defeated outright.

response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, and stable termination. The closed FCSTM adds an Off->Terminate edge and a leaf Terminate with no outgoing transition, which is not present in NL/PlantUML author source at all (PlantUML only has Terminate marked 'final' after Off->Terminate, matching source). The key behavioral finding is that Operate->Off is guarded by R45RouteToken==7, which is only set on the keyOff-triggered exits from Idle/AcceleratingOrCruising/Braking, so the NL2 keyOff endpoint requirement (Operate->Off triggered by keyOff) is realized only indirectly through an internal route-token macro rather than a directly keyOff-triggered Operate-level transition; however per macro-boundary discipline this is a candidate for endpoint lens 1 (contract_structure_contrast), not here. For behavior_consequence, I focus on: (1) NL2-ENDPOINT-2 Operate->Off keyOff: exact model shows Operate's own outgoing transition (line 22) has no trigger (triggers=[]) and is guarded internally, so from a behavioral-consequence perspective the reachable trigger path exists via child transitions consuming keyOff and setting the token, then the guarded Operate->Off transition fires -- this is a multi-step routing rather than single edge; I flag this as a wrong_target/mismatched candidate under NL2-ENDPOINT-2 since the direct Operate-scope transition has no keyOff trigger at all (S3 on transition:line:22 would show empty triggers). (2) Terminate is a deterministic reachable leaf with no outgoing transition (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic, verify deadlock check refuted meaning leaf confirmed) - since Terminate is explicitly the final/terminal state per PlantUML 'final' annotation and NL does not establish termination obligations directly, no NL contract addresses this as termination; there is no supplied termination-state contract, so no candidate there per instructions (do not invent baseless termination contract without NL basis) - but the general deadlock at a designated final state is expected behavior, not a violation, so omitted. branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, and stable termination. The closed FCSTM adds an Off->Terminate edge and a leaf Terminate with no outgoing transition, which is not present in NL/PlantUML author source at all (PlantUML only has Terminate marked 'final' after Off->Terminate, matching source). The key behavioral finding is that Operate->Off is guarded by R45RouteToken==7, which is only set on the keyOff-triggered exits from Idle/AcceleratingOrCruising/Braking, so the NL2 keyOff endpoint requirement (Operate->Off triggered by keyOff) is realized only indirectly through an internal route-token macro rather than a directly keyOff-triggered Operate-level transition; however per macro-boundary discipline this is a candidate for endpoint lens 1 (contract_structure_contrast), not here. For behavior_consequence, I focus on: (1) NL2-ENDPOINT-2 Operate->Off keyOff: exact model shows Operate's own outgoing transition (line 22) has no trigger (triggers=[]) and is guarded internally, so from a behavioral-consequence perspective the reachable trigger path exists via child transitions consuming keyOff and setting the token, then the guarded Operate->Off transition fires -- this is a multi-step routing rather than single edge; I flag this as a wrong_target/mismatched candidate under NL2-ENDPOINT-2 since the direct Operate-scope transition has no keyOff trigger at all (S3 on transition:line:22 would show empty triggers). (2) Terminate is a deterministic reachable leaf with no outgoing transition (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic, verify deadlock check refuted meaning leaf confirmed) - since Terminate is explicitly the final/terminal state per PlantUML 'final' annotation and NL does not establish termination obligations directly, no NL contract addresses this as termination; there is no supplied termination-state contract, so no candidate there per instructions (do not invent baseless termination contract without NL basis) - but the general deadlock at a designated final state is expected behavior, not a violation, so omitted. (3) Event consumer coverage for keyOff is fully reachable across Idle/AcceleratingOrCruising/Braking - satisfied, omit. (4) Root reachability for Operate and Off both proved reachable - satisfied, omit. I therefore emit one candidate for NL2-ENDPOINT-2 focusing on the missing direct keyOff trigger on the Operate-scope transition, using S3 evidence since the trigger set on transition:line:22 is empty despite the contract requiring a keyOff-triggered transition.

stage_receipts.reason: Three segments establish: (1) initial entry to Operate on power-on and a transition group among Operate's substates (Idle, Accelerating/Cruising, Braking), (2) two explicit endpoint transitions triggered by start/keyOff signals between an implicit off state and Operate, and (3) a within-Operate transition group among substates based on actions like accelerating/braking/stopping. Contracts preserve containment, initial-entry, transition endpoints/groups, and triggers without inventing progress obligations for every state. NL1 and NL3 both describe transitions among Operate's substates; NL3 refines/restates NL1's substate transition semantics with explicit action-based conditions, so I treat NL3's group as the authoritative substate-level group while NL1 contributes the Operate initial-entry, substate containment, and the power-on-to-Operate endpoint.
